whoAmI.title: Who am I?
paragraphs: **Data scientist with two years of professional experience** in commercial analytics, data analysis and CRM at RCM Electrical Cables. I hold a **bachelor's degree in Physics from the Federal University of Paraná (UFPR)** and spent an **international research period in computational neuroscience** at the University of Lethbridge (Canada).

My academic path has been geared toward technology: in collaboration with the Pharmacology department, I carried out a **fine-tuning project for image segmentation models** of trigeminal ganglion neurons, applying computer vision and image processing to extract morphometric properties such as area and diameter. The goal was to build an automated research tool with quantifiable error that **turns hours of manual work into seconds**, enabling further studies on the mechanisms of chronic headache. The first results were presented at the **International Headache Congress (IHC) 2025** in São Paulo, and the paper is currently **under peer review at the journal Neuroinformatics**.

While still an undergraduate, I was a special student in the graduate course on **Deep Learning**, took subjects such as **Algorithms and Data Structures I** and **Statistics**, and served as project manager at the junior enterprise [Mathmorphosis](https://www.instagram.com/mathmorphosis/), where I **led the team at [UFPR's 1st Data Hackathon](https://ufpr.br/eventos/hackathon-ia/)**, where we took **Top 3**.

contact.title: Contact
contact.text: I'm especially interested in **interdisciplinary problems**, whether they span different departments of a company or pharmacology, neuroscience and physics. :)

items.title: Commercial Analytics Platform — RCM Electrical Cables
items.description: **I designed and built, from scratch**, an analytics platform for a manufacturer with low data maturity: an **auditable daily pipeline over millions of records** and years of history, a customer-risk model combining business rules with LRFM and sentiment analysis (NLP/LLM), and **revenue forecasting with Prophet**. **It was adopted by the executive board and the sales team**.

items.title: Analytics REST API — RCM Electrical Cables
items.description: I designed and developed a REST API with a modular, domain-based architecture (MVC), exposing **203 analytics endpoints** consumed by the company's internal systems (CRM) **without changing the business logic**. I standardized the response contract, automated coupling tests and documented everything with Swagger.

items.title: Institutional Evaluation Platform — UFPR's 1st Data Hackathon
items.description: **I led a 3-person team** that built, **in 5 days**, a visualization platform for real data from UFPR's institutional evaluation surveys, featuring a sentiment index and opinion-balance charts. We were one of 5 finalist teams out of more than 10 entrants and **placed in the Top 3**; **the university considered the solution for future use** on its platforms.

items.title: Fine-tuning Cellpose-SAM for Neuron Segmentation
items.description: **First author of a paper under peer review at Neuroinformatics**. I adapted a cell-segmentation foundation model (Cellpose-SAM) to detect and measure neurons in histology images, raising AP@50 (Average Precision) **from 0.129 to 0.747 (almost 6×)** and reaching **an F1 of 0.849** and a recall of 0.881 with **only 31 images** and 1,801 annotated objects. The result is an automated tool with quantifiable error for morphological studies, supporting research into the mechanisms of chronic headache.

items.title: Theoretical extension to stochastic regimes in complex-valued neural networks (CVNNs)
items.description: Ongoing research supervised by **Prof. Roberto Budzinski** in the Department of Neuroscience at the University of Lethbridge.

items.title: This portfolio — context engineering applied to a site
items.description: I built **this site by directing a coding agent through specification**, not ad-hoc prompts. I wrote **9 context documents** (~1,000 lines) defining layout, palette, buttons, background and translation, with a clear rule for which one wins when two specs contradict each other. The agent only executed after reading the context and presenting a plan. Every time it had to **depart from a spec, the reason was logged** in `DECISIONS.md`.
